q: 1. In order to measure the flow with a venturimeter, it is installed in
options: any direction and in any location
explain: A venturimeter works accurately in any orientation as long as the Bernoulli equation accounts for the change in elevation (Z).

q: 2. Coefficient of resistance is the ratio of
options: area at vena contracta to area of orifice
loss of head in the orifice to the head available at exit
explain: Coefficient of resistance (Cr) relates the energy loss due to friction to the available kinetic head.

q: 3. A jet of water discharging from a 40 mm diameter orifice has a diameter of 32 mm at its vena contracta. The coefficient of contraction is
explain: Cc = Area of jet / Area of orifice = (32/40)² = 0.8² = 0.64.

q: 4. The theoretical velocity of jet at vena contracta is
explain: Derived from Bernoulli's equation (v = √2gh), assuming no losses.

q: 5. An orifice is said to be large, if
options: the size of orifice is large
the velocity of flow is large
the available head is more than 5 times the height of orifice
the available head is less than 5 times the height of orifice
explain: If head H < 5d, the pressure variation across the orifice is significant, and it is classified as a 'large orifice'.

q: 6. The discharge through an external mouth piece is given by
explain: The average Cd for an external mouthpiece is 0.855, significantly higher than a simple orifice (0.62).

q: 7. An internal mouthpiece is said to be running free if the length of the mouthpiece is ............ the diameter of the orifice.
explain: In a Borda's mouthpiece (internal), if the length is less than twice the diameter, the jet of liquid does not touch the sides, and it is said to be 'running free'.

q: 8. The discharge through a convergent mouthpiece is ............ the discharge through an internal mouthpiece of the same diameter and head of water.
explain: A convergent mouthpiece has a $C_d$ near 1.0, while a Borda's mouthpiece running free has a $C_d$ of 0.5. Thus, the discharge through the convergent one is roughly double.

q: 9. The discharge over a rectangular notch is ............
explain: The standard formula for discharge over a rectangular notch is $Q = \frac{2}{3} C_d \cdot b \sqrt{2g} \cdot H^{3/2}$.

q: 10. The error in discharge (dQ/Q) to the error in measurement of head (dH/H) over a triangular notch is given by ............
explain: By differentiating $Q = kH^{5/2}$, we get $dQ/Q = 2.5 (dH/H)$.

q: 11. When the coefficient of discharge (Cd) is 0.623, then the general equation for discharge over a rectangular weir is ............
explain: Substituting $C_d = 0.623$ and $g = 9.81$ into the Francis formula $ rac{2}{3} C_d \sqrt{2g}$ yields the constant 1.84.

q: 12. The Cippoletti is a ............ weir.
explain: A Cippoletti weir is a trapezoidal weir with a side slope of 1 horizontal to 4 vertical (1:4).

q: 13. A weir, generally, used as a spillway of a dam is ............
explain: An Ogee weir is shaped to follow the profile of the lower nappe of a ventilated jet, making it the most efficient and common shape for dam spillways.

q: 14. When the water level on the downstream side of a weir is above the top surface of a weir, the weir is known as ............
explain: A weir is considered submerged or drowned when the water level on the downstream side is higher than the crest of the weir.

q: 15. According to Manning's formula, the discharge through an open channel is ............
explain: Manning's formula for velocity is $v = M \cdot m^{2/3} \cdot i^{1/2}$. Therefore, $Q = A \cdot M \cdot m^{2/3} \cdot i^{1/2}$.

q: 16. The discharge through a channel of trapezoidal section is maximum when ............
options: width of channel at the top is equal to twice the width at the bottom
depth of channel is equal to the width at the bottom
the sloping side is equal to half the width at the top
the sloping side is equal to the width at the bottom
explain: A trapezoidal section is most economical when the length of the sloping side is equal to half of the top width.

q: 17. The instrument used for measuring the velocity of flow is known as ...............
explain: While venturi and orifice meters measure discharge (Q), the pitot tube is specifically designed to measure point velocity (v).

q: 18. An orifice is an opening in a vessel with ...............
options: closed perimeter of regular shape through which water flows
the water level of the liquid on the upstream side below the top of the orifice
prolonged sides having length of 2 to 3 diameters of the opening in thick wall.
explain: An orifice is defined as a closed-perimeter opening through which fluid flows for measurement or discharge purposes.

q: 19. Short tube mouthpiece will not run full at its outlet if the head under which the orifice works, is ...............
options: less than 12.2 m of the water
more than 12.2 m of the water
equal of 12.2 m of the water
explain: If the head exceeds a certain limit (~12m), the negative pressure at the vena contracta becomes too high, causing the jet to separate and not run full.

q: 20. If H is the difference of liquid levels on two sides of an orifice (width b, depth d), the discharge through the orifice will be ...............
explain: The standard discharge formula for a small orifice is Q = Cd * Area * √(2gH), where Area = b * d.

q: 21. The width of a weir with end contraction, is ...............
options: equal to the width of the channel
less than the width of the channel
half the width of the channel
explain: A weir with end contractions has a crest length shorter than the channel width, causing the water stream to contract horizontally.

q: 22. If S is the length of the crest, H is the height of water source of a weir whose length is L and discharge is Q m³/sec, the velocity of approach Va is ...............
explain: The velocity of approach is the flow velocity in the channel leading to the weir, calculated as Discharge (Q) divided by the Flow Area (Length L × Total Depth [Head H + Crest Height S]).

q: 23. The discharge through a V-notch weir varies as ...............
explain: The discharge formula for a triangular notch is $Q =  rac{8}{15} C_d 	an(	heta/2) \sqrt{2g} H^{5/2}$.

q: 24. The ratio of the percentage error in the discharge and percentage error in the measurement of head over a triangular notch, is ...............
explain: Since $Q \propto H^{5/2}$ for a triangular notch, $ rac{dQ}{Q} =  rac{5}{2}  rac{dH}{H}$.

q: 25. Discharge over an ogee weir remains the same as that of ...............
explain: An ogee weir is designed to follow the lower profile of a nappe from a sharp-crested weir; therefore, its discharge characteristics are ideally the same as those of a sharp-crested weir.

q: 26. An orifice is taken as large if ...............
explain: In practice, if the depth of the orifice ($d = H_2 - H_1$) is greater than about one-third of the head ($H$), it is treated as a large orifice.

q: 27. the inlet length of a venturimeter ...............
options: is equal to the outlet length
is more than the outlet length
is less than the outlet length
explain: The diverging (outlet) section of a venturimeter is made longer than the converging (inlet) section to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss.

q: 28. Venturimeter is used to measure
explain: A venturimeter is a device based on Bernoulli's principle used specifically for measuring the rate of flow (discharge) through a pipeline.

q: 29. Orifice-meter is used to measure
explain: Similar to a venturimeter, an orifice-meter is a cheaper alternative used to measure the discharge or rate of flow in a pipe by creating a pressure drop.

q: 30. An orifice is known as large orifice when the head of liquid from the centre of orifice is
options: more than 10 times the depth of orifice
less than 10 times the depth of orifice
less than 5 times the depth of orifice
explain: If the head of liquid (H) is less than 5 to 10 times the depth of the orifice (d), the velocity varies significantly across the orifice, classifying it as a large orifice.

q: 31. The co-efficient of discharge (Cd)
options: for an orifice is more than that for a mouthpiece
for internal mouthpiece is more than that external
for a mouthpiece is more than that for an orifice
explain: Mouthpieces generally have a higher Cd (around 0.82 for external) compared to a sharp-edged orifice (around 0.62) because they reduce the contraction of the jet.

q: 32. Orifices are used to measure
explain: An orifice is an opening in a vessel used primarily to control or measure the rate of flow (discharge) of a fluid.
